modes.name: uncited_policy_claim
modes.definition: The reply states a policy rule or a policy-based verdict (payouts, returns, refunds, cancellations), including an eligibility verdict taken only from the order's refund_eligible flag, without citing a policy identifier.
modes.product_change: Prompt and retrieval: look up the relevant policy and cite its identifier in every policy-based answer.
modes.boundary: An eligibility verdict counts even when it comes only from refund_eligible. A reply that reports record facts without a verdict or rule is not this mode. A rule that is wrong or goes beyond the policy text is incorrect_policy_claim. A refund-eligibility field in a list of record fields is a record fact; a sentence such as 'please note this order is not eligible' is a verdict (0150 and 0010 against 0017). A statement that an order can or cannot be cancelled is a verdict.

modes.name: missing_data_not_flagged
modes.definition: A tool result has a null or inconsistent field that the answer depends on (for example delivered_at null on a delivered order, a delivery date before the ship date, a negative price), and the reply either does not say the data is missing or inconsistent, or says so but still gives a verdict that depends on it instead of escalating.
modes.product_change: Prompt instruction: when a required field is missing or inconsistent, treat derived flags such as refund_eligible as unreliable, say what is missing, and escalate; or a data-quality flag in the tool result.
modes.boundary: Applies only when the missing field is in the tool result the reply relies on; a verdict given without a citation but with complete data belongs to uncited_policy_claim.

modes.name: asks_instead_of_acting
modes.definition: The user's request clearly calls for a tool action the agent is allowed to take (search or look up records, issue or queue a refund, escalate to a human), and the agent asks for confirmation or input it does not need instead of taking the action.
modes.requirement_source: SPEC ESC-1, ESC-2 (refunds, escalations); PURPOSE-1 (acts through tools) for searches and lookups
modes.product_change: Prompt instruction: act on a clear request with the matching tool (search_products, issue_refund, escalate_to_human) without asking permission or optional details first.
modes.boundary: Asking for information that is genuinely missing and required by the tool (no order number when several orders match, an ambiguous item) is not this mode. Optional filters (budget, style, store) are not required: search_products works without them. A question that follows a purely informational request (the user asked only whether something is possible) is not this mode, because no action was requested. Against escalation_offered_after_denial: here the agent should act and asks; there it offers an action that should not be offered.

modes.name: incomplete_answer
modes.definition: The reply leaves out a fact from the tool result that the answer requires under RESP-7: an order-status answer without the matching shipped or delivered date, or a partial list that does not say how many records were returned.
modes.requirement_source: SPEC RESP-7 (added 2026-10-28; motivated by annotation ann-mvsy7l4m-ihgk on support-0149)
modes.product_change: Prompt instruction on which order facts a status answer must include.
modes.boundary: A request for a short answer does not excuse a missing status date (RESP-7). Extra detail the question does not need is not required. Applies only to order-status answers and partial lists: a refund, cancellation or return-eligibility reply without a date is not this mode. Filtering a list to answer the question asked (0242 shows the 2 eligible orders of 20) is not a partial list. Against missing_data_not_flagged: here the tool returned the fact and the reply left it out; there the fact is null or inconsistent in the tool result.

modes.name: incorrect_policy_claim
modes.definition: The reply states a policy or permission rule, or a consequence of one, that contradicts or adds to what the policy documents, facts.yaml, or the SPEC access matrix say (for example, that a charge cannot be disputed because the order is not refund-eligible, that refund timing depends on the bank, or that a role cannot search products).
modes.requirement_source: SPEC PURPOSE-1, RESP-1 (policy documents are the source); cw-disputes in this example
modes.product_change: Prompt and retrieval: retrieve the policy that governs the request (disputes, returns, payouts) before stating its rule; do not infer one policy from another.
modes.boundary: The stated rule is wrong or goes beyond the policy text. A correct rule stated without a citation is uncited_policy_claim. Includes verdicts that contradict a store's own return policy, or invent a rule such as 'final sale'. A correct verdict taken from refund_eligible, with no rule stated, is uncited_policy_claim even when the store's policy was never read: the mode judges what the reply says, not how the agent got there.

modes.name: escalation_offered_after_denial
modes.definition: After a tool returns permission_denied, the reply offers escalation (or another route) as a way to obtain the data the caller is not authorized to see.
modes.product_change: Prompt instruction: after permission_denied, explain the refusal without revealing details and do not offer escalation to get the data.
modes.boundary: Opposite of asks_instead_of_acting: there the agent should act and asks; here it offers an action that should not be offered. Escalating a genuine dispute or account change is not this mode.

modes.name: malformed_tool_argument
modes.definition: The agent calls a tool with an argument of the wrong kind or format (for example a store ID where search_products expects a store name, or a store name where find_order expects a product description), and the tool rejects it or returns the wrong records.
modes.requirement_source: SPEC section 4 (TOOL-3 store, TOOL-6 product description); RESP-5 for exposing the internal error
modes.product_change: Tool description and schema: state that store takes a store name; optionally accept a store ID.
modes.boundary: The argument is malformed. A well-formed call for the wrong record (wrong order number) is a different failure. The mode is present when the tool rejects the argument, even if the agent recovers afterwards. Against asks_instead_of_acting: here the agent calls the tool with a wrong argument; there it does not call the tool.
